title: Tampa Bay Rays to face Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series
summary: Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz each hit a two-run homer and Freddy Peralta threw 5 1/3 gritty innings as the Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 of the American League…

image.caption: Tampa Bay Rays players and staff members pose for a photo after defeating the Cleveland Guardians in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series at Tropicana Field on Monday in St Petersburg, Fla. (Mike Stobe/Getty Images)

blocks.text: MLB

Junior Caminero and Yandy Diaz each hit a two-run homer and Freddy Peralta threw 5 1/3 gritty innings as the Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 of the American League Championship Series on Monday night to advance to the World Series for the third time in the franchise's 29 seasons.
Tampa Bay to meet Milwaukee in Game 1 of World Series on Friday
The Rays will face the Milwaukee Brewers in the first matchup in which both teams are seeking their first World Series title since 1980.
Game 1 is Friday night in Milwaukee.
"We got one more bite!" Rays manager Kevin Cash told his team as the clubhouse celebration started.
The loss extended Cleveland's World Series championship drought to 78 years.
"I couldn't be more proud of our group," Guardians manager Stephen Vogt said. "It just hurts. It stings. Really felt like we had a team to go and just weren't able to get there."

items: Rasmussen shines as Rays beat Guardians in Game 5 to take a 3-2 ALCS lead

blocks.text: On the 18-year anniversary of their first AL pennant in 2008, the Rays jumped ahead 2-0 in the second inning on Richie Palacios' two-run double and clinched it with closer Bryan Baker on the mound.
The Guardians wouldn't give up and had the go-ahead run at first base in the eighth when Kevin Kelly struck out Brayan Rocchio to leave the bases loaded after two runs scored.

Peralta, the ALCS MVP, allowed one run and five hits to earn his second win of the series in his third appearance. He pitched six scoreless innings to win Game 2 and got two critical outs in relief in Game 4.

"His velocity was so high out of the gate, you were wondering how much he was going to be able to maintain it," Cash said. "But couldn't be more impressed with the way he continued to take deep breaths and just make pitch after pitch for us."

A sellout crowd of 40,230 fans waved yellow-and-blue rally towels, rang cowbells and chanted "Let's go Rays!" throughout the night at Tropicana Field, which needed major renovations after Hurricane Milton shredded the roof two years ago and caused extensive damage throughout the stadium.

The Rays played their 2025 home games across the bay in Tampa at the New York Yankees' spring training complex, got new ownership before this season and secured a new stadium deal to bear ready in 2029 near the NFL's Buccaneers. They returned to the Trop to win 55 games in the regular season. Only the Brewers had that many home wins this year.
"This is for you!" Caminero yelled to the crowd from a microphone on the field after the game. "Let's go! I can't hear you!"

blocks.text: After sweeping the Yankees in the Division Series, the Rays fell behind the Guardians 0-1 and 1-2 in this series before taking three straight games.

Caminero gave Tampa Bay a cushion with his first career post-season homer in the seventh. The two-time All-Star sent a drive off the left-field foul pole to make it 5-1, becoming the first player to go deep on a splitter by All-Star closer Cade Smith.

Caminero turned around before reaching first base, looked toward his dugout and pounded his chest with both arms, cupped his ear rounding second to hear more cheers, stopped before reaching the plate, pointed into the stands and crossed his arms before crossing home.
The slugger hit 42 homers in the regular season but needed 33 at-bats to get his first in October.

The Guardians answered against Tyler Wells and Ian Seymour by loading the bases on two singles and a walk with two outs. Seymour walked Patrick Bailey to force in one run and hit Angel Martinez with a pitch to force in another. Kelly entered and fanned Rocchio on three change-ups.
"Credit to our guys. It's a gut punch there in the seventh. And our guys came right back," Vogt said. "Our guys never quit. They never stopped fighting. That's who they are."
Diaz, who guaranteed a Game 6 victory through an interpreter on Sunday, gave the Rays another four-run lead with a two-run shot off Hunter Gaddis in the bottom of the eighth.
"I'm really glad he backed it up, that's for sure," Cash said. "We know when Yandy goes, our offence seems to really take off."

Caminero led off the Tampa Bay second with single off opener Shawn Armstrong, who took the loss in his second start in three games. Left-hander Tim Herrin replaced Armstrong. Chandler Simpson reached on a fielder's choice and stole second before Victor Mesa Jr. walked. Simpson advanced to third on Jonny DeLuca's flyout to centre. After Mesa stole second, Palacios looped a double to right-centre for a 2-0 lead.
Armstrong, who was the opener in Game 4, faced the first four batters, becoming the first pitcher in post-season history to start a game after pitching both of the previous two days.
DeLuca's sacrifice fly off Joey Cantillo made it 3-0 in the third but the Rays missed an opportunity to break it open with more runs after they loaded the bases with no outs.
Nathaniel Lowe's RBI single in the sixth drove in Cleveland's first run.
